inputs.name: Dawkins half-frequency times (dominant, recessive)
inputs.cite: Q50 = H3 q1 (secondhand, as posted by Day); parameters haldane.dawkins_figures

day.reading: even 642,888 generations for one base pair exceeds the available time; for 20 million the factor is 87,916,307

critic.reading: a single-allele time to half frequency is not a fixation time for a parallel process; x 20M is serial
critic.holds: the factor is 20M x t_site / G_eff, the sequential form (M-706); the doubling is unexplained (x2) and the recessive choice multiplies the answer by 27.4 over the dominant one

notes: The arithmetic reproduces: 642,888, 4.3958 (4.4), 87,916,307.7 (printed 87,916,307, truncated; 88 million with 4.4). The Dawkins figures are secondhand (book not retrieved), so the record does not test whether 11,739 and 321,444 follow from s = 0.001: their starting frequency is not held. Three choices set the answer: the doubling from half frequency (x2, not explained in the post), recessive over dominant (x27.4; the dominant case doubled is 23,478 generations, 6.2 times inside G_eff) and the serial multiplication by 20 million (M-706, M-115).
